title: ACA s. 8 — Power to refer parties to arbitration where there is an arbitration agreement

content.overview: A judicial authority before which an action is brought in a matter which is the subject of an arbitration agreement shall, if a party so applies not later than the date of submitting the first statement on the substance of the dispute, refer the parties to arbitration unless it finds that prima facie no valid arbitration agreement exists.
content.glance: Mandatory reference to arbitration on timely application unless prima facie no valid arbitration agreement exists.
content.study: Section 8 is mandatory when its conditions are met. After the 2015 Amendment and Vidya Drolia, the court applies a prima facie standard: when in doubt, refer. Only a clear case of non-existence of a valid arbitration agreement or clear non-arbitrability justifies refusal.

sections.heading: Mandatory reference
sections.body: The judicial authority shall refer the parties to arbitration when the statutory conditions are satisfied.

sections.heading: Timing of the application
sections.body: The application must be made not later than the date of submitting the first statement on the substance of the dispute.

sections.heading: Prima facie standard
sections.body: Refuse reference only if prima facie no valid arbitration agreement exists or the dispute is clearly non-arbitrable; when in doubt, refer.

provisions.title: Power to refer parties to arbitration

cases.name: Vidya Drolia v. Durga Trading Corporation
cases.facts: Reference on arbitrability and the standard of review under sections 8 and 11.
cases.issue: What is the scope of judicial examination under section 8 after the 2015 amendments?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Sections 8 and 11 have the same ambit; the court refers unless a party establishes a prima facie case that no valid arbitration agreement exists or the dispute is clearly non-arbitrable. When in doubt, refer.
cases.holding: Referral is the rule; refusal is exceptional and requires a clear prima facie case.
cases.relevance: Governing standard for section 8 reference applications.

cases.name: P. Anand Gajapathi Raju v. P.V.G. Raju
cases.facts: Application under section 8 seeking reference of a pending suit to arbitration.
cases.issue: What conditions must be satisfied for a reference under section 8?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Section 8 is mandatory when the statutory conditions are met: arbitration agreement, timely application before the first statement on the substance of the dispute, and identity of subject-matter.
cases.holding: Reference ordered on satisfaction of the statutory conditions.
cases.relevance: Foundational authority on the mandatory character of section 8.

questionsAndAnswers.question: When must a court refer parties to arbitration under section 8?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: When a party applies not later than the first statement on the substance of the dispute and the court does not find that prima facie no valid arbitration agreement exists.
questionsAndAnswers.explanation: Section 8 as interpreted in Vidya Drolia.
